meta.title: BIM Validator — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: BIM Validator: open source tool that checks IFC models against IDS requirements such as NL BIM Basis ILS and the RVB BIM Norm. View the findings in 3D and export them as BCF. As a Windows app, a Python package or on your own server.

header.label: In development · IFC validation
header.title: BIM Validator
header.tagline: Check IFC models against IDS requirements
header.desc: Load an IFC model, choose NL BIM Basis ILS, the RVB BIM Norm or your own IDS file and see per element what is missing. View the errors in 3D and pass them on to your team as BCF issues. As a Windows app, as a Python package or on your own server.

alt.overview: The BIM Validator with an IFC model in 3D and the results of a check against NL BIM Basis ILS
alt.rvb: A check against the RVB BIM Norm, with the model tree on the left and the failed specifications on the right
alt.bcf: The BCF issues from a check, ready to export as a BCF file
alt.project: Opening a project from your own computer or from connected project storage
alt.video: Demo video of the BIM Validator

notice.text: Not production-ready yet: this tool is in development. You can try it out, but do not use it for real project work yet. Report what you run into on GitHub.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From IFC model to findings
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

ids.title: Check your model against the requirements
ids.desc: Choose NL BIM Basis ILS (12 specifications), the RVB BIM Norm (26 specifications) or an IDS file of your own. For each specification you see how many elements pass and which ones fail, with the GlobalId, the IFC class and the reason.

viewer.title: See in 3D where it goes wrong
viewer.desc: The model sits next to the results. Click a finding and the viewer zooms in on the element, with its properties alongside. Section planes let you look inside the building, and you can load several models at once.

bcf.title: Findings as BCF issues
bcf.desc: Turn a failed specification into a BCF issue with a viewpoint and export the list as a BCF 2.1 file. You can also open a BCF file, view the viewpoints, change the status and export it again. Comments and authors are kept.

local.title: An app, a package or a server
local.desc: The Windows app has the validation server built in, so your model stays on your own computer. Keep projects locally or in connected project storage. To check models in a script or pipeline, use the Python package or the HTTP API.

ids.title: IDS validation
ids.desc: Check an IFC model against any IDS file, with pass or fail per element.

nlbim.title: NL BIM Basis ILS v2
nlbim.desc: 12 specifications, covering among other things storey names, NL-SfB, spaces, load-bearing structure, fire resistance and materials.

rvb.title: RVB BIM Norm v1.1
rvb.desc: 26 specifications from the Dutch Government Real Estate Agency, such as project data, site location, storeys, spaces and NL-SfB per element type.

custom.title: Your own IDS file
custom.desc: Load the requirements of your own project or organization.

schema.title: IFC2X3 and IFC4
schema.desc: Both schemas, from any BIM package that exports IFC.

reports.title: Reports in JSON and HTML
reports.desc: Save the results to share them or process them further.

viewer.title: 3D viewer
viewer.desc: Orbit, pan and zoom through the model, with a cube to pick the viewing direction.

tree.title: Model tree and properties
tree.desc: Browse from project to element and view info, property sets, quantities and type.

section.title: Section planes
section.desc: Section planes in X, Y and Z that you select and drag in the 3D view.

themes.title: Five themes
themes.desc: Light, dark, Blueprint and two high-contrast themes.

bcfexport.title: BCF 2.1 export
bcfexport.desc: Findings with viewpoint and snapshot in a single BCF file.

bcfimport.title: Open BCF files
bcfimport.desc: Open a .bcf or .bcfzip file, jump to the viewpoint and change the status.

bcfkeep.title: Nothing gets lost
bcfkeep.desc: On export, topic IDs, authors, comments and images are kept. Importing again does not overwrite your local issues.

cli.title: Command line
cli.desc: ifc-validate model.ifc --ids nl-bim for batches, scripts and CI pipelines.

python.title: Python library
python.desc: Use the validation core on its own in your own code, without the app.

api.title: HTTP API
api.desc: Upload a model, follow the validation as a job and fetch the BCF when it is done.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.desc: Let an AI assistant check models, list standards and create reports locally.

container.title: On your own server
container.desc: A container with the web interface and the API that runs as a regular user.

status.q: Can I use the BIM Validator yet?
status.a: You can try it out: there are pre-releases for Windows and a Python package. The tool is still in development, so do not use its results as the only check in real project work yet.

cost.a: Nothing. The source code is free to use under the MIT license. The IfcOpenShell components that run the validation are licensed under LGPL-3.0 or later.

ids.a: The Information Delivery Specification is an open buildingSMART standard for writing down information requirements in an XML file that software can read. Such a file says, for example, that every wall must have an NL-SfB code and a fire resistance. The validator checks per element whether the model meets it.

compliance.q: Does my model meet the standard if everything passes?
compliance.a: Not necessarily. The bundled IDS files for NL BIM Basis ILS and the RVB BIM Norm are the project's own interpretation of those standards. Passing means the model meets that interpretation, not every requirement of the source. Requirements that cannot be expressed in IDS need a separate assessment.

data.a: The 3D viewer shows the model on your own computer. For validation the model goes to the validation server: in the Windows app that is a server running on your own computer, in an installation of your own it is your own server.

platforms.q: Does it work on macOS or Linux?
platforms.a: There is no installer for macOS or Linux yet. The Python package (Python 3.11 or 3.12) does work, with the command line and the library, and you can build the server as a container yourself.

size.q: How large can a model be?
size.a: Expect about ten times the file size in memory. A 200 MB model therefore needs around 2 GB of RAM.

bcfms.q: How does it work with BCF Manager Studio?
bcfms.a: Export the findings as a BCF file and import it into BCF Manager Studio or any other package that reads BCF 2.1. A direct connection is planned.
